items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: And at that session we had Benny Carter, we had Jimmy Harrison, we had Jabbo Smith, we had Sidney DeParis and this bass player I’m telling you about.

ctx.x: Black Swan Records? He was with Black Swan?

No, I don’t know if it was Black — I don’t know the name of the record right now, see. I don’t know if it was Okeh, Black Swan or Emerson or what. In that category, yes. But that was my first record. But the next record I made it was with this band that I worked so long at Small’s Paradise. That was on Victor Records. And at that session we had Benny Carter, we had Jimmy Harrison, we had Jabbo Smith, we had Sidney DeParis and this bass player I’m telling you about. And at that session I made all the arrangements…

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: there were 3 saxophones -- Benny Whittet, Benny Waters and Benny Carter. Three Bennys in the saxophone section.

ctx.x: Now when did the arranging come in, and let's bring that up to 1928, sort of, or up to the point where you joined Fletcher Henderson.

Actually, I started arranging when I was with Charlie Johnson's orchestra at the Small's Paradise. I started arranging by writing saxophone choruses, you know, for 3 saxophones, because that's what we had then, and there were 3 saxophones -- Benny Whittet, Benny Waters and Benny Carter. Three Bennys in the saxophone section.

And I used to write the saxophone choruses, you know, the rhythm section, because they knew all the chord changes and I knew the chord changes, but I didn't know how to do anything else. And I decided I wanted to arrange. I started studying what they called 'stock arrangements' -- arrangements by Don Redman, Archie Blyer, Arthur Lang, Walter Paul; I guess, Jimmy Dale, Jack Mason ... these are the names I remember, and I used to layout the parts on the floor and study them. And I started arranging just like that;…

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I'm working with a great band with Charlie Johnson, such guys as Jimmy Harrison, all that kind of stuff - Sidney de Paris, Edgar Sampson, Benny Carter, Billy Taylor

ctx.x: I remember the song. You see, I'll tell you about this King Oliver, 'cause I'd get in the same arguments in Europe, you know. Rather lot of people in Europe says I didn't record with - no, no, they didn't say I didn't because they couldn't say that. They said "Did you really record with King Oliver?" So I used to be drinkin', you know, I used to be drinkin' and I heard that so much - "Did you record with King-", you know. At least it was such a great band, and I'm working with a great band with Charlie Johnson,…
